# From making calls to delivering results: Tool interfaces, reliability, and collaboration contracts

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-29 · 49 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

Toolformer learns when to call, SWE-agent designs action interfaces, and RATED addresses reliability among relevant tools. AutoGen programs messaging, MetaGPT structures role deliverables, and World of SWEcraft checks collective output on hidden downstream dependencies. Any layer can fail; a valid call format is not end-to-end completion.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

Axes: Whether improvement targets call policy, interaction interface, tool selection, or team protocol · Whether feedback comes from language loss, actual execution, structured deliverables, or hidden downstream tasks · Whether collaboration state is dialogue, explicit intermediate artifacts, or persistent repository assets · How failures and resources are included in delivery metrics

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Choosing a tool does not establish that it works

Toolformer filters calls by prediction gains, supplying policy-training signal. SWE-agent organizes executable interfaces and their return formats. RATED separates semantic relevance from recent reliability. Record willingness to call, valid format, actual interface success, and task completion independently. Relevance does not compensate for a broken service, and successful calls do not supply counterfactual rewards for unchosen tools.

Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md) · [RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics](../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en.md)

### Messaging protocols, intermediate artifacts, and ecosystem effects

AutoGen programs who replies and when to continue or stop. MetaGPT further constrains role inputs and outputs with SOP deliverables. World of SWEcraft widens evaluation to long-term maintenance across repositories: package tests can pass while downstream consumers break. These methods address control, information handoff, and external effects respectively. Counts of messages, roles, or artifacts do not replace downstream evidence. Long-lived collaboration needs persistent assets and session budgets rather than an indefinitely growing chat.

Sources: [AutoGen](../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en.md) · [MetaGPT](../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en.md) · [World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds](../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

Meta's official retrieval-programs repository is now verifiable, updating RPL's prior open-source record. The main repository is CC-BY-NC4; vendored retrieval and training components retain their licenses. Public code does not make the local typed grammar cover arbitrary Python, cross-turn state, neural retrieval, or RL. No source was copied and the existing L1 evidence did not change.

Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why might RATED deprioritize a tool whose API call Toolformer selected as useful? {#cross-usefulness-versus-reliability}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Training selection shows that returned values helped prediction, not continued service availability or stable argument behavior. RATED first restricts to relevant tools, then updates reliability from selected tools' actual successes, errors, and timeouts using discounting. Training usefulness and current executability are separate, and one failure cannot assign negative rewards to all untried tools.

    **Illustrative example:** An exchange-rate API can help training and time out repeatedly in deployment. It remains relevant, but actual reliability should affect future choices.

    Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics](../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en.md)

### If AutoGen already has programmer and tester roles, why do MetaGPT and SWE-agent emphasize structured deliverables and ACI? {#cross-message-protocol-versus-artifact}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Role names specify responsibilities, while AutoGen's replies and stopping organize interaction. MetaGPT specifies deliverables for requirements, design, and implementation to reduce drift in free chat. SWE-agent defines concrete viewing, editing, and testing actions. Control, information contracts, and action interfaces are complementary, not interchangeable.

    **Illustrative example:** A tester can know when to reply without a clear interface specification. Even with a complete spec, an imprecise editing command can change the wrong code.

    Sources: [AutoGen](../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en.md) · [MetaGPT](../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md)

### Why does World of SWEcraft use hidden downstream packages after MetaGPT or SWE-agent repository tests pass? {#cross-local-tests-versus-downstream}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Own tests cover maintainer-visible contracts and may only improve visible microbenchmarks. API changes can break real consumers. Hidden downstream checks install frozen release versions to assess collective delivery. Retain failed packages in speed accounting and declare strict/carry semantics. A local micro pass does not establish ecosystem capability.

    **Illustrative example:** Renaming an argument and updating library tests can still break consumers using the old name; downstream checks reveal it.

    Sources: [MetaGPT](../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md) · [World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds](../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en.md)

### Why retain local RPL component limitations after finding the official repository? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Source completeness and execution fidelity are different. Published training code does not make the existing constrained SDK execute the full policy, neural retrieval, or distillation. Future integration needs separate cost, execution, and license checks.

    **Illustrative example:** Learning the official training entry point does not turn local retrieval-program syntax tests into multi-hop QA evaluation.

    Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en.md)
